name: snort
why: A classic intrusion detection engine with rule-based packet inspection, a good door into how network traffic is actually read.

brief.what_it_is: Snort is an open source network intrusion detection and prevention system. It inspects network packets against a set of rules that describe malicious activity, and it generates alerts when packets match. It can run inline to stop matching packets, or work as a packet sniffer or packet logger for traffic debugging. Input is live network traffic or pcap files (the README runs it on a.pcap); output is alerts and logs. The Homebrew formula also installs snort2lua, which converts Snort 2.X configs and rules to the new format, plus show_flows, u2boat, u2spewfoo, and appid_detector_builder.sh.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage describes Snort as the foremost open source intrusion prevention system, meant to be downloaded and configured for personal and business use alike. The README frames Snort 3 as the next generation Snort IPS, with new features and all Snort 2.X features and bug fixes.
brief.how_it_works: Rules define malicious network activity, and Snort matches captured packets against them to raise alerts. Rules come in a Community Ruleset, freely available and QAed by Cisco Talos, and a Snort Subscriber Ruleset, developed and approved by Cisco Talos and delivered in real time to subscribers. The Snort 3 config is a Lua file (snort.lua), and the README says the rules are pulled in automatically once an Oinkcode is entered.

brief.install_notes: Dependencies per the README: CMake, DAQ (github.com/snort3/libdaq) for packet IO, dnet, flex 2.6.0 or newer, g++ 7 or newer or another C++17 compiler, hwloc, LuaJIT, OpenSSL, libpcap, PCRE2, pkg-config, and zlib. Optional extras are in a separate snort3_extra repo. Config: set any needed variables at the top of snort.lua and snort_defaults.lua before using Talos rules or configs. For rules, sign up on snort.org for an Oinkcode, which pulls the rules into your instance; the Registered ruleset is free, and the Subscriber ruleset is paid. From the Homebrew caveats (not the README): on macOS, Snort needs read permission on the BPF devices, set with sudo chmod o+r /dev/bpf*, or with a startup item that does this at boot.
brief.standout: Snort 3 is configured with a scriptable Lua file, supports multiple packet threads, autodetects services for portless configuration, and has pluggable components. The README also includes a libFuzzer fuzzing setup with coverage reports, which is less common for a long-running IDS.
brief.status: unknown. I found no release date or last-commit date in the pages I read. The README still points to the 3.0.0 tarball snort-3.0.0-a3 and says 'Version = 3.0.0 (Build 250)', so parts of it look dated. The snort.org homepage is active: it says 'Snort 3 is here!', lists Snort 3.1.0.0 setup guides, and shows a 2026 copyright.
brief.caveats: Windows support is listed only as a roadmap item, and proxy mode and hardware offload are also roadmap. Rule syntax changed from Snort 2: content sub-options need comma separation, buffer selectors must come before content, and pcre buffer selectors were removed. The most current rules need a paid Subscriber ruleset. Build needs a C++17 compiler and several libraries, and fuzzing needs Clang. The README says the how-and-why documentation is thin, and the manual is the main reference. I did not check the license terms beyond the homepage link to the Snort License, so I cannot say more about licensing.
